investigacion.base:
**The question is still open.** The 2026 World Series begins on October 23, three days from now (October 20, 2026). No games have been played, so nothing points to Yes or No yet. The opponent is now set as the **Tampa Bay Rays**, so the Guardians are out.

**Resolution sources**
- I couldn't open the Baseball-Reference 2026_WS page directly. Since no games have been played, it would show no result.
- The Metaculus FAQ just defines "credible sources" and has nothing about this series.
- Wikipedia (updated October 20) lists the series as "upcoming", with both teams at 0 wins. The series is scheduled to begin on October 23, with a possible Game 7 scheduled for October 31.

**Recent news**
- **NLCS, finished about October 15–16:** The Brewers advanced to their second overall World Series after sweeping the two-time defending champion Los Angeles Dodgers. They won their first National League pennant in franchise history. Before that, they beat the Padres in four games in the NLDS.
- **ALCS, finished October 19:** Tampa Bay beat Cleveland 4-2 in the ALCS.
- **Regular-season records:** Milwaukee Brewers (0) Pat Murphy 103–59 (.636)... Tampa Bay Rays (0) Kevin Cash 98–64 (.605). The Brewers have home-field advantage.
- **Head-to-head:** The Brewers took two of three at American Family Field and outscored the Rays by a combined 16-7. That was the second series of the season.
- **Payrolls:** the Competitive Balance Tax payrolls for the Brewers and Rays are $154.7 million and $112.9 million respectively.
- **History:** neither team has won a title. Milwaukee lost the 1982 World Series to St. Louis in seven games. Tampa Bay lost in 2008 (Phillies) and 2020 (Dodgers).

**Betting odds**
- ESPN, about October 18, before the ALCS ended: Milwaukee Brewers -185 Tampa Bay Rays +300 Cleveland Guardians +500.
- -185 works out to roughly 65% for the Brewers, including the bookmaker's margin. Their head-to-head price against the Rays is probably similar or a little higher.
- Preseason they were 14th-best 35-1 odds.
- I didn't find any Polymarket or Kalshi prices, so I can't give a market price or trading volume.

**Base rates**
- Since 1903, the team with home-field advantage has won roughly 55–60% of World Series. The team with the better record has a similarly modest edge.
- Bookmaker favorites of around -180 win about 60–65% of the time.

**Schedule (all games 8 p.m. ET on FOX)**

It will be the second World Series held at the Trop, so Games 3–5 are at Tropicana Field.

The series will be decided by October 31 at the latest. The Brewers are the betting favorites, but there's no result yet.

criterios: This question resolves YES if the Milwaukee Brewers are the winning team of the 2026 World Series (Major League Baseball's championship series, a best-of-seven played between the Brewers and the American League champion, with Games 6 and 7, if needed, scheduled for October 30 and 31, 2026). It resolves NO if the American League champion (the Cleveland Guardians or Tampa Bay Rays) wins the 2026 World Series instead. Resolution is based on the official 2026 World Series result as reported at https://www.baseball-reference.com/postseason/2026_WS.shtml or, if unavailable, by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions).
letra_pequena: If the World Series is abandoned without a champion being crowned (so that no team is recorded as the 2026 World Series winner), the question is annulled.
razonamientos:
(a) **Time left:** The World Series starts October 23 and should be decided by October 31—within 11 days.

(b) **Status quo:** No games have been played. Milwaukee is the betting favorite, but there is no current winner.

(c) **Reference class:** World Series teams with home-field advantage have historically won roughly 55–60% of the time. Milwaukee’s quoted odds suggest a somewhat higher chance, though the implied probability includes bookmaker margin.

(d) **No scenario:** Tampa Bay wins four games, perhaps by splitting the first two in Milwaukee and taking advantage of its three scheduled home games.

(e) **Yes scenario:** Milwaukee’s stronger regular-season form carries through, and it wins four games.

(f) **Resolution technicality:** The question concerns the *official series winner*, not who leads at any intermediate point. If the series is abandoned without a champion, the question is annulled rather than resolved No.

Probability: 62%

Probability: 62%

(a) **Time left:** The series starts October 23 and ends by October 31 at the latest. The outcome will be known in about 4–11 days.

(b) **Status quo:** No games have been played and the series is 0–0. The Brewers enter as favorites, so the status-quo lean is a Brewers win.

(c) **Reference class and base rate:**
- World Series favorites priced around -170 to -185 win roughly 60–64% of the time once the bookmaker's margin is removed.
- Teams with home-field advantage have won about 55–60% of World Series.
- MLB playoff series are high-variance, so even clearly better teams rarely exceed about 65% in a best-of-seven.

(d) **No scenario:** The Rays' pitching depth and bullpen shut down the Brewers' offense. They steal one of Games 1–2 in Milwaukee and win the middle games at Tropicana Field, taking the series in 5 or 6.

(e) **Yes scenario:** The Brewers carry their playoff form (7–1 in the NLDS and NLCS combined) into the series. They hold serve at home and win at least one game in Tampa, clinching in 5–7 games.

(f) **Technicalities:** The question resolves YES only if the Brewers are the official 2026 World Series winner. If the series is abandoned with no champion, the question is annulled. Otherwise it is a straightforward outcome with no notable technicalities.

**Estimate:** The odds imply roughly 60–63% for Milwaukee after removing the margin. Their better record, home field and regular-season edge over the Rays support this, but the underlying variance of a seven-game series keeps it modest.

Probability: 60%
